sections.h2: Which Harrison office takes a Clare County deed?
sections.html:
The combined County Clerk and Register of Deeds office sits at 255 W. Main Street, Harrison, MI 48625. Mail goes to PO Box 438. Reach staff at 989-539-7131 or by fax at 989-539-6616, and the county site gives clerk@clareco.net as the email address.

In Clare County one elected office holds both jobs, so the person who files circuit court papers and issues marriage licenses also keeps the land records. Harrison has been the county seat since 1877, when the seat moved from Farwell. A seller in Clare, Farwell, Harrison or any lake community around them sends the deed to the same counter. Phone first for counter hours.

sections.h2: How did Clare County and its records come about?
sections.html:
The Michigan Legislature created the county from part of Michilimackinac County in 1840 under the name Kaykakee County, and renamed it Clare County in 1843. A series of other counties administered it until its own government was organized in 1871. Farwell served as the first county seat before the seat moved to Harrison in 1877.

That history explains why older Clare County property descriptions may trace back through several jurisdictions. The county covers 564 square miles of land and is counted as part of both Northern and Central Michigan. The Clare-Gladwin Regional Education Service District serves students in the county, and the county is served by several public school districts, so a buyer's questions about schools go to the district the house sits in.

As in other Michigan counties, the county records deeds and mortgages, while cities and townships handle tax assessment, building and zoning, and street maintenance. Ask the township or city office about assessments, and ask the Harrison office about what is on the record.

Wooded acreage and lake cottages make up much of the housing stock around Harrison and Farwell, and the Census counted 22,209 housing units in the county in 2025 against 12,521 households. That gap tells a seller that many neighbors are part-year owners, which can matter when a deed has several co-owners who sign in different states. Each signer's printed name must match the acknowledgment, so gather every signature page before the package goes to the recorder.

sections.h2: What does the Clare County Register of Deeds handle in a home sale?
sections.html:
It records the deed that moves ownership to your buyer and the mortgage that goes with it. The same office holds earlier deeds, land contracts, discharges and liens, so a title search on a Clare County house begins and ends in these books.

The county's homepage also lists the clerk as the official abstractor, a role that matters when a seller needs a title history on an older parcel. Clare County sits among large state forests, and a seller with an older wooded parcel can ask for the deed history early so closing is not held up.

  • Bring the original signed deed, not a photocopy.
  • Include the fee, a return envelope and any certificate the deed type requires.
  • Keep a copy of the recording stamp for your closing file.

sections.h2: What does Clare County bill for recording a deed?
sections.html:
The base charge set by Michigan is $30.00 a document, with page count irrelevant. MCL 600.2567 sends $5.00 of that fee into the register of deeds' automation fund and adds $3.00 for each additional instrument an assignment or discharge covers.

Copies run a dollar a page and a certification is $5.00. A requested records search costs 50 cents per year searched with a $5.00 floor, and filing some other paper is $1.00. Charter counties may use a different schedule, so verify the total with the Clare office by phone.

sections.h2: How is Michigan transfer tax shown on a Clare County deed?
sections.html:
The deed must print the total value of the real property, or an affidavit of value goes with it. Both the county act (MCL 207.504) and the state act (MCL 207.525) say so.

With the value printed, the arithmetic is short. The county takes 55 cents and the state takes $3.75 on every $500 slice of price, partial slices counted whole. A $133,800 sale, which matches the Census median home value in Clare County, spans 268 slices: $147.40 for the county and $1,005 for the state. If real and personal property sell together, naming each value separately confines the tax to the real property. Ask the office how it collects the tax so payment arrives with the deed.

sections.h2: What belongs on page one of a Clare County deed?
sections.html:
The first printed line must name the recordable event in a single statement, such as warranty deed or quit claim deed. MCL 565.201 bars recording an instrument signed after April 1, 1997 when that statement points to more than one event.

  • Keep 2.5 inches clear at the head of page one.
  • Keep half an inch clear on every other side, on every page.
  • Print in 10-point type or larger, black ink, on white stock of 20-pound weight or more.
  • Attach nothing that falls outside letter or legal dimensions.

Once an instrument is received and recorded, the statute presumes it complies, so a clean first page protects you later.

sections.h2: When does a Clare County deed need treasurer certification?
sections.html:
A deed that conveys title with warranty covenants, and a land contract, needs county treasurer certification under MCL 211.135. The certificate says whether tax liens or tax titles exist and confirms payment of the taxes for the five years that precede the deed.

If the register of deeds refuses to receive a deed for lack of certificates, the office notes that fact on the instrument, and the person presenting it must obtain the certificate before trying again. Plan for that trip to the treasurer when you are scheduling a closing, because the deed cannot be recorded without it.

sections.h2: What do Census figures say about Clare County homes?
sections.html:
Clare County is a lower-priced market. The table lists the Census Bureau's figures.

Clare County at a glance, from federal survey data

Share of homes held by owners86.9%

Population rose 2.2% from the 2020 base to the 2025 estimate. In the 2020 count, 39.1% of the 21,818 housing units stood vacant. Workers spend 29.9 minutes getting to work on average, the longest commute among the four counties compared, and the county is nearly all land, with 564 square miles of ground and 11 of water. A typical home sells for less here than in the lakefront counties to the north.

faqs.q: Is the Clare County Register of Deeds a separate office from the clerk?
faqs.a: No. The County Clerk and Register of Deeds offices are combined in Clare County, and both operate from 255 W. Main Street in Harrison.

faqs.q: How do I phone the Clare County office?
faqs.a: Dial 989-539-7131, or fax 989-539-6616. Letters go to PO Box 438, Harrison, MI 48625. Ask about counter hours before you deliver a deed.

faqs.q: What is the standard recording fee in Clare County?
faqs.a: The statutory fee is $30.00 per document, long or short. Add $3.00 for each extra instrument on an assignment or discharge, and $5.00 if you want a certified copy.

faqs.q: How do I figure the transfer tax on a Clare County sale?
faqs.a: Divide the price by $500, round up, then multiply by $0.55 for the county and by $3.75 for the state. A $150,000 sale is 300 slices, so $165 county tax plus $1,125 state tax, or $1,290 together.

faqs.q: Can I mail a deed to the Clare County Register of Deeds?
faqs.a: Yes. Send the signed original, the exact fee and a return envelope to PO Box 438, Harrison, MI 48625. Confirm the amount by phone first so the deed is not held for a short payment.
